capture.final_message:
Treat each `Iff` as an equivalence between two independently valid universal facts.

- For the first `Iff`, use the zero-preservation axiom of `IsAbsoluteValue` for the right side. For the left side, characterize failure of `AbsoluteValue.IsNontrivial`: if no nonzero element has value different from `1`, then the absolute value agrees pointwise with `AbsoluteValue.trivial`—at zero by zero-preservation, and away from zero by the failed nontriviality condition. Function extensionality then gives equality. The converse follows from a nontriviality witness separating the two maps. Decidable equality with zero is what makes the trivial absolute value available.

- For the second `Iff`, the left side is exactly the triangle inequality supplied by `IsAbsoluteValue`. For the right side, apply the triangle inequality to
  \[
  a=(a+b)+(-b),
  \]
  obtaining
  \[
  |a|\le |a+b|+|-b|=|a+b|+|b|.
  \]
  Then rearrange in the ordered ring to conclude
  \[
  |a|-|b|\le |a+b|.
  \]
  The only substantive auxiliary fact is invariance under negation, `abv (-b) = abv b`; the ordered-domain/no-zero-divisor assumptions support the standard proof that an absolute value sends `-1` to `1`.
